key_insight: Fusing camera images with IMU data using a lightweight bidirectional cross-attention module plus an adaptive gating layer yields more robust, generalizable road surface classification across diverse environmental conditions; the paper also provides a new multimodal dataset to benchmark this setting.
problem_solved: Existing road surface classification methods struggle to generalize beyond narrow operational conditions because of limited sensing modalities and datasets lacking environmental diversity. This work addresses both limits by supplying a diverse camera–IMU dataset and an efficient fusion framework that adapts to noisy or degraded inputs.
method: Curate a synchronized multimodal dataset of camera frames and IMU readings covering varied road types, lighting and weather conditions (benchmark for RSC).
Fuse visual and inertial features via a lightweight bidirectional cross-attention module to let each modality inform the other.
Apply an adaptive gating layer that dynamically weights modalities to suppress noisy sensors and emphasize reliable cues, followed by a compact classifier for on-device deployment.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical fusion architecture and dataset to build RSC models that generalize to real-world variability and run efficiently on edge platforms—reducing failures in predictive maintenance and autonomous systems.

paper_title: A New Dataset and Framework for Robust Road Surface Classification via Camera-IMU Fusion
paper_authors: Willams de Lima Costa, Thifany Ketuli Silva de Souza, Jonas Ferreira Silva, Carlos Gabriel Bezerra Pereira, Bruno Reis Vila Nova
